clue.text: Feeble course I must enter with the others

parts.note: a path is a course or route

indicators.note: the letter I is to go into the abbreviation for 'and the rest'

parts.note: etc (et cetera) means 'and the others'

explanation.surface: A weak course of study that I am obliged to join along with everyone else.
explanation.definitionFit: Pathetic in the sense of pitifully weak or inadequate is a direct synonym for feeble.

clue.text: To gain energy, a partner taking a soothing juice

indicators.note: the partner takes on the second A after it
the letter for energy is added inside the other pieces

parts.note: a lover is a romantic partner
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A partner sips something soothing to get a boost of energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloe vera sap is the gel prized for calming burns and irritated skin.

clue.text: Made haste to protect animal under stress

indicators.note: the word for hurried wraps around the animal to shield it

parts.note: hared means ran fast, made haste
an ass is a donkey

explanation.surface: Someone rushed to shield a creature in distress.
explanation.definitionFit: Harassed means worn down and stressed by constant demands.

clue.text: Fashionable society around west London?

indicators.note: the word for society surrounds the letter for west

parts.note: the ton is an old term for high society

explanation.surface: High society living around the west of London.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks London as an example: going 'up to town' meant going to London.
explanation.definitionFit: London is an example of a large urban place, and Londoners speak of it simply that way.

clue.text: Vehicle takes a run through county

indicators.note: the A and R go into the county name

parts.note: Cavan is a county in the Republic of Ireland
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A vehicle makes a drive across a county.
explanation.walkthrough: AR goes after the C of CAVAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A caravan is a towed vehicle fitted out for living in on holiday.

clue.text: Feature of fat person suggesting good health?

definitions.text: Feature of fat person suggesting good health?

parts.words: Feature of fat person suggesting good health?
parts.note: a fold of flesh under the jaw of a heavy person; the second reading is a toast, 'chin-chin', a chin said twice to wish good health

explanation.surface: A trait of an overweight person that hints at their wellbeing.
explanation.walkthrough: The toast 'chin-chin' wishes good health, and it is a chin said twice.
explanation.definitionFit: An overweight person often has a second roll of flesh beneath the jaw.

clue.text: Where life is hectic, stop eating on running track

parts.note: to fast is to stop eating
each runner on an athletics track has a lane

explanation.surface: Busy lives where people skip meals and run on the track.
explanation.definitionFit: Life in the fast lane is the idiom for a hectic, high-pressure lifestyle.

clue.text: Sly, always about to betray our side first

indicators.note: the pronoun for our side comes at the front

parts.note: we means our side, us

indicators.note: the word for always goes around the word for betray

parts.note: ay (aye) is an old word for always
to sell someone out is to betray them

explanation.surface: A shifty person who would always sell out our side first.
explanation.definitionFit: Weaselly describes someone cunning and evasive, like a weasel, so it means sly.

clue.text: Paul, for example, worried for the French renegade

indicators.note: one piece standing in for another signals a swap of letters in the word for Paul's role

parts.note: St Paul was an apostle
le is the French masculine 'the'
ate, as in 'what's eating you?', means worried or troubled

explanation.surface: Paul, perhaps, fretted on behalf of the French turncoat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' means 'in place of': ATE replaces LE at the end of APOSTLE.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostate abandons a faith or cause, the very definition of a renegade.

clue.text: Not entirely natural athlete, one may be found in the library

definitions.text: one may be found in the library

indicators.note: the word for natural is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a born leader is a natural one
a rower is a sporting athlete in a boat

explanation.surface: A natural athlete who is only partly that, apparently a library regular.
explanation.definitionFit: Library users who take books out on loan are borrowers, so one is a typical library visitor.

clue.text: Most advisable to enter a call for help for material needing removal

indicators.note: the word for most advisable goes into the A plus distress call

parts.note: SOS is the distress signal
the best course is the most advisable one

explanation.surface: Seemingly advice on how best to put out a distress call about hazardous stuff.
explanation.definitionFit: Asbestos is the notorious carcinogenic mineral insulation that has to be stripped out of old buildings.

clue.text: Banter in itself contains one warning signal

indicators.note: the Latin phrase holds the other pieces within it

parts.note: per se is Latin for 'in itself'
I is the Roman numeral one
a flag can be waved as a warning signal

explanation.surface: Light teasing that has a warning flag built into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Persiflage is light, frivolous mockery or teasing talk, a synonym for banter.

clue.text: Writer considered inept, page needing rework

parts.note: felt means believed or considered

indicators.note: the letters of inept plus the page letter must be reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: An author thought to be clumsy, whose page has to be rewritten.
explanation.walkthrough: INEPT plus P is rearranged to TIPPEN; 'Writer' suggests an author but is a pen.
explanation.definitionFit: A felt-tip pen is an instrument for writing, so a writer in the crossword sense.

clue.text: Turning to drink, holding one large container

indicators.note: the reversed word keeps the numeral inside it
turning round means the word for drinking is read backwards

parts.note: to lap is to drink as a cat does
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone taking to drink while clutching a big vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A pail is a bucket, a sizeable open vessel for carrying liquids.

clue.text: Paper taking party line repeatedly: child's play

parts.note: a rag is slang for a newspaper
a do is a party

indicators.note: the letter for line is given more than once, here twice

explanation.surface: A newspaper toeing the party line again and again: easy stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'child's play' looks like the idiom for something easy; here it means a toy a child plays with.
explanation.definitionFit: A rag doll is a soft cloth toy, something for a child to play with.

clue.text: Pulling this, perhaps, strains hard — I sympathise

parts.note: to rick a joint is to strain it
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
'aw' is an exclamation of sympathy

explanation.surface: Hauling something strains the body, and the speaker feels for them.
explanation.definitionFit: A rickshaw is a light cart drawn by a person running between its shafts, so it is something pulled.

clue.text: Cross-dressing in something transparent, almost, just the thing for party?

indicators.note: the cross-dressing word goes inside the shortened material
the word for the see-through material loses its last letter

parts.note: glass is a transparent material
drag is clothing of the opposite sex

explanation.surface: Cross-dressing in an almost see-through outfit, ideal for a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross-dressing' looks like part of the picture but is the inserted piece; 'almost' drops the final S.
explanation.definitionFit: Glad rags are one's best clothes, put on for a party or night out.

clue.text: Nervous about one extremely brief trembling

indicators.note: the word for nervous goes around the other pieces

parts.note: shy means timid or nervous
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the word for extremely is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: very means extremely

explanation.surface: Someone nervous about a moment that is very brief and quivering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' trims the last letter of the word for extremely; 'about' puts that and I inside the word for nervous.
explanation.definitionFit: Shivery describes someone shaking or quivering with cold or fear.

clue.text: Woman one confused with vicar

indicators.note: the letters of one and vicar are mixed up into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman mistaken for the local vicar.
explanation.definitionFit: Veronica is a woman's given name, so a woman in crossword terms.

clue.text: Embarrassed about playwright in a state of nature again

definitions.text: in a state of nature again

indicators.note: the colour word goes around the playwright

parts.note: a red face shows embarrassment
Oscar Wilde was the Irish playwright

explanation.surface: Someone red-faced about a dramatist, back in the wild.
explanation.definitionFit: Land that is rewilded has been returned to its natural, uncultivated state.

clue.text: Go wrong, tearing into stuff with sharp teeth

indicators.note: the word for erring rushes into the middle of the word for stuff

parts.note: to sate is to stuff or glut
to err is to go wrong

explanation.surface: Things go wrong as something rips into material with its sharp teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Serrate means notched along the edge like a saw blade, toothed.

clue.text: Cold and bleak for crop

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
raw weather is bleak and chilly

explanation.surface: Cold, bleak weather bad for growing a crop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crop' suggests farming, but it is the pouch in a bird's gullet.
explanation.definitionFit: A craw is the crop of a bird or insect, a pouch in the gullet for food.

clue.text: Exclusive group start to enter through low gate

indicators.note: the first letter of enter goes in among the letters of the poor attendance

parts.note: a gate is the attendance at a sports match, so a low one is a thin crowd

indicators.note: the beginning of the word enter supplies its first letter

explanation.surface: A select clique gets in by way of a low gate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gate' looks like a barrier, but it is the number of spectators at a match; E goes after TH.
explanation.definitionFit: The in-crowd is the fashionable clique that others want to join.

clue.text: Club performer's band doubling power, beginning to rock

indicators.note: the P already in the word for band is doubled by adding a second one

parts.note: a stripe is a band of colour

indicators.note: the start of the word rock gives its first letter

explanation.surface: A club musician's group doubles its power as it starts to rock.
explanation.walkthrough: Doubling the P in STRIPE gives STRIPPE; R follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A stripper is an entertainer who undresses on stage at a nightclub.

clue.text: Leap from aeroplane (its rear)

parts.note: a ... is a ...-powered aeroplane
the rear of the aeroplane, the final letter of that word, is E

explanation.surface: Jumping out of a plane from the back.
explanation.definitionFit: A jeté is a ballet jump from one foot to the other.

clue.text: Notices about sheep spurned by old natives

indicators.note: the word for notices goes around the sheep remnant

parts.note: ads are advertisements, notices

indicators.note: the letter for old is rejected, leaving the sheep without it

parts.note: a merino is a breed of sheep

explanation.surface: Notices concerning sheep that elderly people turned their backs on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spurned by old' strips the O from the sheep breed; 'about' wraps the notices round what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Amerinds are the indigenous peoples of the Americas, its native inhabitants.

clue.text: Row of pawns kept by instinct beside a rook

indicators.note: the article and rook letter sit next to the other piece

parts.note: R is the chess notation for rook

indicators.note: the word for pawns is held inside the word for instinct

parts.note: a gut feeling is instinct
chess pieces are called men, and pawns are men

explanation.surface: A chess line of pawns guarded by intuition next to a rook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like the chessboard rank, but it is a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A row, rhyming with cow, is a noisy quarrel or dispute.

clue.text: Announced I am able to deploy extremely pretty girl

indicators.note: spoken out loud, the phrase for being able is heard as a different pair of words

parts.note: 'I can' means I am able

indicators.note: the outermost letters of deploy are used

explanation.surface: Someone declaring they can make use of a very attractive woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Eye candy is slang for someone attractive to look at, especially a pretty young woman.
